![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251141/assets/fc485a3c47295e08c917d1c9a2e90df0a0d6eaa931f4df23e17700da1536ca6e.png)

In the quadrilateral $OMNP$ shown above, find the measure of $∠N.$
question.worked_solution:
A quadrilateral has $n=4$ sides. Therefore, the sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral must be 

$$
\begin{aligned}{180}^{∘}\cdot (n-2) & ={180}^{∘}\cdot (4-2) \\  & ={180}^{∘}\cdot 2 \\  & ={360}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding up the internal angles and solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠M+m∠N+m∠P+m∠O & ={360}^{∘} \\ {104}^{∘}+(10x-{4}^{∘})+{104}^{∘}+{76}^{∘} & ={360}^{∘} \\ 10x+{280}^{∘} & ={360}^{∘} \\ 10x & ={80}^{∘} \\ x & ={8}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠N & =10x-{4}^{∘} \\  & =10({8}^{∘})-{4}^{∘} \\  & ={76}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
